cases.why: The THREE-part form `Qualifier.Enum.Member`, with the qualifier being the declaring standard module. This is the form the task is really about - a member is supposed to be reachable as [[Lib.]Enum.]Value - and nothing in the corpus or the docs establishes whether the module name may occupy that first slot. If this is legal the resolver needs a third level; if not, the first slot is for type libraries only and the design is simpler.

The two-part form with the MODULE rather than the enum as qualifier. VB6 lets a module qualify its Public members generally, and an enum member is hoisted into the module's namespace - so this asks whether the hoisting is real membership or something weaker. Distinguishes 'the member is a module-level constant' from 'the member is only reachable through its enum'.

A deliberate nonsense control for the previous two. If the qualifier chain is a general dotted lookup this might resolve; if the levels are fixed it cannot. Predicting illegal, and its value is entirely in bounding how general the real rule is.

Is an enum member a CONSTANT or merely a pre-set variable? HexIDE hoists each member with DefineVariable, so today it is assignable and a program can silently overwrite vbRed. Predicting illegal - VB6 should refuse the assignment - and if so the hoist is using the wrong mechanism.

Assigning a value no member declares. VB6 enums are Longs with names, not closed sets, so this should be accepted and print 999 - but if it is REFUSED then a typed variable carries real range enforcement and the interpreter would have to model it. Predicting legal.

What a variable DECLARED as the enum type reports. A member's own TypeName is measured `Long`; this asks whether a declared variable keeps the enum name or collapses to Long as well. The answer decides whether the interpreter needs a distinct enum-typed slot or can treat the declaration as a Long alias.

Two enums declaring the same member name. Members are hoisted into the module namespace, so this is a collision - VB6 may refuse the duplicate outright, or allow it and make only the qualified form usable. HexIDE currently lets the second silently overwrite the first in a program-wide table, which is the same shape as issue #180 for Types, so the answer decides whether that is one defect or two.

Where an Enum may be DECLARED. The grammar reaches enumerationStmt from moduleBodyElement, so a procedure-local Enum should already be refused - but the grammar also reaches `block` from the module body, and this confirms the boundary rather than assuming it. Predicting illegal.
